architecture_decisions.recommendation: Modified error message parsing to split only on the first colon instead of all colons
architecture_decisions.rationale: The previous implementation used `message.split(':')` which would split on ALL colons in the message. This caused error messages containing multiple colons (like 'With: multiple: colons') to be incorrectly truncated after the second colon. By using `indexOf(':')` and slicing the string, we preserve the full error context after the first colon while maintaining the separation between the error summary and field-specific errors.
alternatives_considered: Using regex with a non-greedy match (e.g., /^([^:]*):(.*)$/)
Adding a configuration option to control colon handling
Changing the error message format entirely to use a different separator

architecture_decisions.recommendation: Added comprehensive test suite for the error parsing function with edge cases
architecture_decisions.rationale: Created a new test file to verify the fix handles various scenarios: messages without colons, single colon messages, multiple colon messages, error path formatting, and grouping of similar errors. This ensures the fix works correctly and prevents regression. The tests specifically verify the multiple colon case that was previously broken.
alternatives_considered: Adding the test cases to an existing test file
Only testing the specific bug case without broader coverage
Using integration tests instead of unit tests

architecture_decisions.recommendation: Made the `createErrorsFromMessage` function exportable for testing
architecture_decisions.rationale: Changed the function from being module-private to exported (`export function createErrorsFromMessage`) so it can be imported and tested directly. This follows the principle of making pure logic functions testable without requiring complex mocking or UI rendering. It also improves code organization by separating business logic from React components.
alternatives_considered: Keeping the function private and testing through component integration
Moving the logic to a separate utility file
Using dependency injection to make the function testable

architecture_decisions.recommendation: Maintained backward compatibility with existing error message formats
architecture_decisions.rationale: The implementation preserves the existing behavior for messages with zero or one colon while fixing the multiple colon case. Error messages are still expected to follow the format 'summary: field1, field2, field3' where the summary is separated from field errors by a colon. The fix only changes how multiple colons within the field errors portion are handled.
alternatives_considered: Breaking change to require a new error format
Adding version detection to handle old vs new formats

tickets.title: Fix error message truncation for messages with multiple colons
tickets.description: Update the error parsing logic to split only on the first colon instead of all colons, preserving complete error context in toast notifications

implementation_summary:
The implementation addresses a bug where error messages containing multiple colons were being incorrectly truncated in toast notifications. The core fix replaces `message.split(':')` with manual string slicing using `indexOf(':')` to only split on the first colon occurrence. This preserves the full error context after the initial separator while maintaining the existing format where the part before the colon serves as a summary and the part after contains comma-separated field errors.

The solution maintains backward compatibility by not changing the expected error message format. Messages without colons return the full message, single-colon messages split as before, and multiple-colon messages now correctly preserve everything after the first colon. The function was also exported to enable direct unit testing, and a comprehensive test suite was added to verify all edge cases including the specific bug scenario.

This approach follows the principle of minimal change - fixing the specific issue without redesigning the entire error handling system. The fix is localized to the parsing logic and doesn't affect how errors are generated or displayed elsewhere in the system. The test coverage ensures the fix works correctly and prevents regression while documenting the expected behavior for future developers. New files introduced by this change: `packages/ui/src/elements/Toasts/fieldErrors.spec.ts`.
